name: 大理
description: Dali is a picturesque town in Yunnan province, set against the dramatic backdrop of Cangshan Mountains and beside the crystal-clear Erhai Lake. Home to the Bai ethnic minority with 1,000 years of history. Known for cobblestone streets, traditional Bai architecture, and vibrant local culture. A laid-back atmosphere perfect for cycling, hiking, and cultural immersion.
highlights: Erhai Lake - Scenic cycling and views
Three Pagodas of Dali - Buddhist temples
Dali Old Town - Traditional Bai architecture

climate.tips: Spring (March-May) is flower season with mild weather. Autumn (Sept-Oct) has clear skies and comfortable temps. Summer is rainy but green. Winter is dry and sunny but cold. Bring layers - temperature swings daily.

culturalTips.title: Bai Culture
culturalTips.content: Dali is home to the Bai ethnic minority. Respect local customs. The Bai have unique traditions including the 'Three-Angel' dress and tie-dye crafts. March Fair and Raosanling festival are major events.

culturalTips.title: Erhai Cycling
culturalTips.content: Cycling Erhai Lake is the signature experience. 120km around the lake. Start early, bring water and sunscreen. Rent bikes in Dali or Caicun. The eastern shore is less crowded.

culturalTips.title: Mountain Weather
culturalTips.content: Dali's weather changes quickly. Mountains cause localized weather systems. Even in summer, bring a jacket. Rain can appear suddenly. Spring flowers and autumn colors are spectacular.

culturalTips.title: Temple Etiquette
culturalTips.content: When visiting Three Pagodas and temples, dress modestly covering shoulders and knees. Remove hats in temples. Don't point feet at Buddha images. Walk clockwise around pagodas.

culturalTips.title: Bai Tie-dye Culture
culturalTips.content: The Bai are famous for traditional tie-dye (zaran), using natural plant dyes on cotton fabric. Each pattern has symbolic meaning. Zhoucheng village is the center of this craft. Look for butterfly, fish, and flower patterns.

culturalTips.title: Yunnan Tea Culture
culturalTips.content: Yunnan is famous for Pu'er tea. Dali has tea houses where you can experience tea ceremony. The Bai Three Tea Ceremony (sandaocha) represents life flavors: bitter, sweet, and aftertaste. Tea is an important part of local social life.

culturalTips.title: Bai Festivals
culturalTips.content: Major Bai festivals include: March Fair (Sanyuejie) - horse trading and trading fair in Dali; Rao San Ling (Raosanling) - pilgrimage to Three Sacred Places; Torch Festival (Huobajie) - lighting torches to ward off pests. Summer and early autumn are festival seasons.

culturalTips.title: Bai Architecture
culturalTips.content: Bai houses feature white walls, grey tiles, and horse-head roofs. Three-in-one courtyards (sanfang yizhaobi) are typical. Look for the ornate gate towers (jingmei de menlou) and paintings on walls inside courtyards.

culturalTips.title: Bai Traditional Clothing
culturalTips.content: Bai women wear 'Three-Angel' costumes (sandaocha) with white jackets, blue belts, and embroidered shoes. The famous 'Phoenix Crown' headdress symbolizes the phoenix. You can rent costumes for photos in tourist areas.

culturalTips.title: Bai Religion
culturalTips.content: The Bai follow a mix of Buddhism, Taoism, and Benzhu (benzhu) worship - worship of local deities. Every village has a Benzhu temple. The Three Pagodas are important Buddhist sites. Be respectful when observing rituals.

culturalTips.title: Bai Music
culturalTips.content: Bai opera (baiju) combines singing, dancing, and acting. Traditional instruments include the Sanxian (sanxian) and Horse-head fiddle. You can catch performances at Dali Ancient Town or during festivals.

culturalTips.title: Bai Food Culture
culturalTips.content: Bai cuisine features fresh vegetables, mushrooms, and fish. Rushan (rushan) is stretched milk cheese. Bender (liangji) is cold chicken. Try local specialties at markets: Baba (baba) flatbread, Ersi (ersi) rice noodles, and Mi Liangxia (mi liangxia) shrimp-shaped jelly dessert.

culturalTips.title: Bai Silver Crafts
culturalTips.content: Bai silver smithing is famous for intricate jewelry and decorative items. Silver is believed to have health benefits. Popular items include silver bracelets, hair ornaments, and tea accessories. Authentic silver has high purity.

culturalTips.title: Bai Wedding Customs
culturalTips.content: Bai weddings feature unique customs including the 'Jiao Zhai' (jiaozhai) ritual where the bride bites the groom's ear. Wedding feasts are elaborate multi-course affairs. The bride changes into multiple costumes during the ceremony.

culturalTips.title: Erhai Fishing Culture
culturalTips.content: Fishing has been central to Erhai life for centuries. Traditional fishing methods include using cormorants (lusi). Some fishing villages still practice these methods. Fish dishes are staples of local cuisine.

culturalTips.title: Bai Language
culturalTips.content: The Bai language (baiyu) is tonal and completely different from Mandarin. Many locals speak both Bai and Mandarin. Learning a few Bai phrases like 'Ni hao' (hello) and ' Xie xie' (thank you) in Bai will be appreciated.

culturalTips.title: Photography Tips
culturalTips.content: Dali offers excellent photography opportunities: sunrise at Erhai Lake, the pink wall in Xizhou, Cangshan Mountain reflections, and Bai people in traditional clothing. The best light is early morning and late afternoon. Bring a tripod for night shots of the Three Pagodas.

culturalTips.title: Dali Shopping
culturalTips.content: Dali is famous for tie-dye products, silver jewelry, tea (especially Pu'er), and marble. The best shopping is at the morning market in Xizhou and Zhoucheng for tie-dye, and the Foreigners Street in Dali Old Town for silver and souvenirs. Bargaining is expected in markets.

culturalTips.title: Altitude and Health
culturalTips.content: Dali sits at about 1972m elevation. Some visitors may experience mild altitude sickness. Stay hydrated, avoid strenuous activity on arrival, and eat lightly. The medical facilities in Dali are adequate for basic health issues.

culturalTips.title: English in Dali
culturalTips.content: English is limited in Dali outside tourist areas. Learning a few Mandarin phrases helps. Many young people in Dali Old Town and Shuanglang speak basic English. Translation apps are helpful for communicating with older locals.

culturalTips.title: Environmental Awareness
culturalTips.content: Erhai Lake's ecosystem is fragile. Avoid single-use plastics, don't swim in restricted areas, and use eco-friendly transportation. Several initiatives promote lake protection. Be a responsible tourist.

culturalTips.title: Nanzhao Kingdom Heritage
culturalTips.content: Dali was the capital of the Nanzhao Kingdom (738-902 AD), one of the longest-ruling dynasties in Chinese history. The Three Pagodas, Nanzhao Island, and Weishan Ancient Town reflect this heritage. Understanding this history enriches the visit.

culturalTips.title: Yunnan Coffee Culture
culturalTips.content: Yunnan produces some of China's best coffee. Dali has several specialty coffee shops using locally grown beans. Try the Yunnan pour-over at cafes on Foreigners Street. Coffee plantations are nearby and offer tours.

culturalTips.title: LGBTQ+ Friendly Destination
culturalTips.content: Dali has a reputation as one of China's more LGBTQ+ friendly destinations, with a relatively open atmosphere and welcoming vibe. Several bars and cafes cater to the community. The laid-back atmosphere is generally accepting.

culturalTips.title: Digital Nomad Hub
culturalTips.content: Dali has become a popular base for digital nomads and remote workers. Many cafes offer fast WiFi and quiet workspaces. Monthly apartment rentals are affordable. Coworking spaces are available in Dali Old Town.

culturalTips.title: Dali Nightlife
culturalTips.content: Dali has a vibrant nightlife scene around Foreigners Street with bars, live music, and clubs. Shuanglang has a more relaxed evening atmosphere with lake-view bars. Most nightlife closes by midnight on weekdays.

culturalTips.title: Best Time to Visit
culturalTips.content: The best times to visit Dali are March-May (spring flower season) and September-November (clear skies, autumn colors). Summer (June-August) is rainy but green. Winter is dry and sunny but cold. Avoid Chinese holidays when tourist sites are crowded.

attractions.name: 洱海
attractions.description: A beautiful highland lake often called 'Sea of Clouds' offering scenic cycling paths, traditional fishing villages, and stunning mountain backdrops.
attractions.address: Erhai Lake, Dali Bai Autonomous Prefecture
attractions.tips: Rent a bicycle (40-80¥/day) to circle the lake. Start early to avoid tour buses. Best light for photos in early morning.

attractions.name: 大理三塔
attractions.description: Iconic trio of ancient Buddhist pagodas dating back to the 9th century, symbol of Dali's historic Nanzhao Kingdom.
attractions.tips: Visit in morning to avoid tour crowds. Combine with nearby Butterfly Spring in spring. Good photo opportunities from temple courtyard.

attractions.name: 大理古城
attractions.description: A beautifully preserved ancient town with traditional Bai architecture, cobblestone streets, and lively local culture.
attractions.tips: Stay overnight to experience night atmosphere. Early morning before shops open for photos. Explore side alleys for authentic Bai life.

attractions.name: 喜洲古镇
attractions.description: Well-preserved Bai ethnic town famous for its architecture, local markets, and authentic Bai way of life.
attractions.tips: Visit on market day (Friday, Saturday) for authentic experience. Try Baba (Bai flatbread) from vendors. Zhou's compound is worth entrance fee.

attractions.name: 双廊
attractions.description: A serene lakeside village on Erhai Lake's eastern shore, known for scenic beauty, boutique hotels, and photography spots.
attractions.tips: Stay overnight at boutique lakeside hotels. Best sunset views from Nantian. Rent electric bike to explore coastline.

attractions.name: 苍山
attractions.description: A dramatic mountain range behind Dali with hiking trails, ancient temples, and panoramic views of Erhai Lake.
attractions.tips: Take the cable car up for easier hiking. Weather changes quickly - bring layers and rain gear. Hiking trail is well marked but steep.

attractions.name: 巍宝山
attractions.description: A sacred Taoist mountain with ancient temples, hiking trails, and panoramic views of the Dali valley.
attractions.tips: Less visited than Cangshan. Good for hikers seeking solitude. Bring water and snacks. Start in morning.

attractions.name: 蝴蝶泉
attractions.description: A legendary spring surrounded by ancient trees, traditionally associated with butterfly mating season in spring.
attractions.address: Butterfly Spring Park, 20km north of Dali
attractions.tips: Best in April-May when actual butterflies appear. Combine with Xizhou and Erhai Lake cycling. Performance times: 9:30, 11:00, 14:00, 15:30.

attractions.name: 周城扎染
attractions.description: The largest Bai ethnic village famous for traditional tie-dye crafts. Over 90% of residents are involved in tie-dye production.
attractions.tips: Visit morning market on weekends. Try DIY tie-dye experience. Best light for photos in early morning.

attractions.name: 巍山古城
attractions.description: A perfectly preserved ancient city and the birthplace of the Nanzhao Kingdom. Less touristy than Dali Old Town with authentic local life.
attractions.tips: Come for the torch festival (July-August). Try Weishan's famous Nanjiang rice noodles. Start from the south gate.

attractions.name: 南诏风情岛
attractions.description: A small island in Erhai Lake showcasing Nanzhao Kingdom culture with statues, temples, and traditional Bai architecture.
attractions.tips: Combine with Shuanglang visit. Take the boat to the island. Best visited in morning.

attractions.name: 小普陀
attractions.description: A tiny island temple in Erhai Lake with a small pagoda, one of the most photographed spots in Dali.
attractions.tips: Best at sunrise for photography. Can feed seagulls from the boat. Combine with cycling the eastern shore.

attractions.name: 洗马潭
attractions.description: A high-altitude alpine meadow and marsh at Cangshan Mountain, accessible by cable car with stunning views.
attractions.tips: Take the cable car up. Weather changes rapidly - bring warm layers. Best visited in summer for wildflowers.

attractions.name: 天龙洞
attractions.description: Ancient Buddhist cave temple with colorful statues and carvings dating back to the Nanzhao Kingdom period.
attractions.tips: Combine with Cangshan hike. The cave is smaller than it looks from outside. Good for shelter if raining.

attractions.name: 洱源西湖
attractions.description: A beautiful lake area with wetland scenery, lotus fields, and traditional Bai fishing villages. Less crowded than Erhai Lake.
attractions.tips: Best in summer for lotus. Take a boat tour through the waterways. Good for cycling combined with nearby temples.

attractions.name: 喜洲海舌生态公园
attractions.description: A peninsula extending into Erhai Lake, offering 180-degree views of the lake and Cangshan Mountains.
attractions.tips: Best at sunrise or sunset. Very crowded on weekends. Combine with Xizhou Baba tour.

attractions.name: 大理州博物馆
attractions.description: A modern museum showcasing Dali's history from Nanzhao Kingdom to present, with artifacts and interactive exhibits.
attractions.tips: Good for rainy days. English descriptions available. Combine with nearby Erhai Lake walk.

attractions.name: 寂照庵
attractions.description: A serene Buddhist temple famous for its thousands of potted flowers and peaceful atmosphere.
attractions.tips: Try the vegetarian food. Very peaceful. Wear comfortable shoes for the walk up. Bring cash for donations.

attractions.name: 张家花园
attractions.description: A restored Bai courtyard garden showcasing traditional Bai architecture, with tea tasting and cultural performances.
attractions.tips: Book tickets online for discounts. Combine tea tasting and performance. Good for learning about Bai culture.

attractions.name: 大理学院情人坝
attractions.description: A scenic embankment near Dali University popular with students and couples, offering beautiful Erhai Lake views.
attractions.tips: Best at sunset. Nearby small restaurants and cafes. Popular with local students.

attractions.name: 鹿卧山
attractions.description: Hillside viewpoint between Dali Old Town and Erhai Lake, offering scenic views of both.
attractions.address: Between Dali Old Town and Erhai
attractions.tips: Best at sunset for photos with both town and lake. Can be crowded on weekends.

attractions.name: 乌龙坝草甸
attractions.description: Highland grassland area with windmills, offering scenic views and photography opportunities.
attractions.tips: Less visited, great for escaping crowds. Bring food and water. Best in spring and summer.

attractions.name: 崇圣寺
attractions.description: Chongsheng Temple was the royal temple during the Dali Kingdom period, forming one entity with the Three Pagodas. It is the most magnificent Buddhist architectural complex in Dali, with splendid halls and solemn Buddha statues, showcasing the Buddhist culture of the Nanzhao and Dali Kingdoms.
attractions.address: 1.5 km north of Dali Ancient Town
attractions.tips: It is recommended to visit together with the Three Pagodas. The temple offers vegetarian meals. Going in the afternoon allows you to see the reflection of the Three Pagodas.

attractions.name: 洋人街
attractions.description: Foreigner Street is the most famous pedestrian street in Dali Ancient Town, named for the large number of foreign tourists who gathered there in early years. The street is lined with shops, cafes, bars, and craft stores, epitomizing the leisure life of Dali.
attractions.tips: It's liveliest in the evening, with many live music performances. You can try Dali specialties like grilled milk fan (ru shan).

attractions.name: 五华楼
attractions.description: Wuhua Tower is a landmark of Dali Old Town, originally built during the Nanzhao period as the state guesthouse of the Nanzhao Kingdom. The current building is a reconstruction; climbing it offers a panoramic view of Dali Old Town, with views of Cangshan Mountain and Erhai Lake in the distance.
highlights: Panoramic view of the old town
attractions.tips: The best time to climb the tower is in the evening, to see the sunset and the old town's night scenery. There are exhibitions inside the tower to visit.

attractions.name: 大理古城墙
attractions.description: Dali Old Town City Wall was first built in the Ming Dynasty and served as an important defensive structure for Dali Old Town. The wall is well-preserved, with south and north gates, and the gate towers are great spots to enjoy the old town scenery.
attractions.tips: You can walk from the South Gate to the North Gate, enjoying the old town scenery along the way. The city wall is a great place for photos.

attractions.name: 南诏风情岛
attractions.description: Nanzhao Customs Island is the largest island in Erhai Lake. It features the Nanzhao Palace and the Benzhu Culture Square, showcasing the history of the Nanzhao Kingdom and Bai culture, making it an important site for understanding Dali's history.
attractions.address: In the middle of Erhai Lake, Shuanglang Town, Dali City
attractions.tips: You need to take a boat to the island; it is recommended to check the weather in advance. The island has beautiful scenery, perfect for taking photos.

attractions.name: 白族扎染博物馆
attractions.description: The Bai Tie-Dye Museum showcases the traditional tie-dye craft of the Bai people in Dali. This national intangible cultural heritage has a history of over a thousand years. Visitors can learn about the tie-dye process and try it themselves.
attractions.address: Zhoucheng Village, Xizhou Town, Dali City
attractions.tips: You can try tie-dye yourself and make your own work to take home. Zhoucheng Village is a professional tie-dye village.

attractions.name: 喜洲古镇
attractions.description: Xizhou Ancient Town is a representative of Bai culture in Dali, preserving a large number of traditional Bai residential buildings. Among them, Yan's Grand Courtyard is the most famous Bai architectural complex. The ancient town is also renowned for Xizhou baba (a type of flatbread).
highlights: Bai 'three rooms and one screen wall' architectural style
attractions.tips: Be sure to try the freshly baked Xizhou baba (stuffed flatbread), available in both sweet and savory flavors. Going in the morning lets you see scenes of local life.

attractions.name: 苍山索道
attractions.description: The Cangshan cable car is the most convenient way to tour Cangshan Mountain. Taking the cable car takes you directly to the mountainside, offering magnificent views along the way. At the summit, you can overlook the entire Erhai Lake and Dali Old Town.
attractions.tips: The temperature at the summit is relatively low, so it's advisable to bring a jacket. The cable car may suspend operations in bad weather, so check the forecast in advance.

attractions.name: 苍山瀑布
attractions.description: The Cangshan waterfalls are a major attraction, with the most famous being Qingbi Stream and the Seven Dragon Maiden Pools. The waterfalls cascade down from the heights of Cangshan, splashing water everywhere, creating a beautiful picture with the green vegetation of the mountain.
attractions.address: Within Cangshan Scenic Area, Dali City
attractions.ticketPrice: Included in the Cangshan Mountain admission ticket
attractions.tips: The rainy season (June-September) offers the most spectacular waterfalls. It's recommended to wear non-slip shoes as the mountain paths are steep.

attractions.name: 大理玫瑰花田
attractions.description: The rose fields in Dali are a newly emerging tourist attraction in recent years. Large expanses of roses bloom at the foot of Cangshan Mountain, forming a stunning scene with the distant Cangshan and Erhai Lake, making it a popular spot for photos.
attractions.address: Yinqiao Town and other areas, Dali City
attractions.tips: The rose blooming season is from April to June, and the afternoon light is best. You can buy local specialties like rose jam.

attractions.name: 严家大院
attractions.description: Yan Family Grand Courtyard is the most famous Bai ethnic residential complex in Xizhou Ancient Town. Built in the late Qing and early Republic period, it consists of multiple 'three-bay with one screen wall' and 'four-courtyard with five skywells' layouts, making it an outstanding example of Bai architectural art.
attractions.address: Sifang Street, Xizhou Town, Dali City
attractions.tips: It is recommended to hire a guide to explain the features and cultural significance of Bai architecture. The courtyard also features Bai three-course tea performances.

attractions.name: 石宝山
attractions.description: Shibao Mountain is located in Jianchuan County, known for its grottoes and Danxia landforms. The mountain houses numerous grotto statues from the Nanzhao and Dali Kingdom periods, earning it the title 'Southern Dunhuang' and serving as precious material for studying Nanzhao history.
attractions.address: Shibao Mountain, Jianchuan County, Dali Prefecture
attractions.tips: It is quite far from Dali city, so self-driving or hiring a car is recommended. The mountain paths are steep, so wear comfortable shoes.

attractions.name: 凤羽古镇
attractions.description: Fengyu Ancient Town is a Bai ethnic town in Eryuan County, Dali Prefecture, known as the 'Museum of Bai Architecture'. The town preserves many Bai residential buildings from the Ming and Qing dynasties, offering a tranquil environment away from the city's hustle and bustle.
attractions.address: Fengyu Town, Eryuan County, Dali Prefecture
attractions.tips: Fewer tourists, allowing you to experience authentic Bai life. It is recommended to drive there.

attractions.name: 诺邓古村
attractions.description: Nuodeng Ancient Village is the oldest village in northwestern Yunnan, famous for salt production. The village retains many Ming and Qing dynasty buildings, including salt wells, temples, and residences, making it a great place to experience the ancient village culture of western Yunnan.
attractions.address: Nuodeng Town, Yunlong County, Dali Prefecture
attractions.tips: Nuodeng ham is very famous and a must-try. The village is built on a hillside, so there is a lot of walking; wear comfortable shoes.

attractions.name: 海东艺术村
attractions.description: Ha Dong Art Village is located on the east bank of Erhai Lake, and is Dali's emerging art hub, attracting many artists and literary youths to settle and create here. The village has various art studios, cafes, and guesthouses.
attractions.tips: In the evening, you can watch the sunset by Erhai Lake, which is very beautiful. Suitable for literary youths to check in.

attractions.name: 才村码头
attractions.description: Cai Village Pier is the nearest Erhai cruise pier to Dali Ancient City. From here, you can take a boat to tour Erhai Lake. Around the pier, there are many lake-view guesthouses and cafes, making it a great place to enjoy the scenery of Erhai Lake.
attractions.tips: Caicun Pier is most beautiful in the evening, where you can watch the sunset over Erhai Lake. You can take a boat tour to explore the lake.

attractions.name: 洱海观景台
attractions.description: The Erhai Lake viewing platform is located on the high ground of the eastern shore, making it the best spot to overlook the panoramic view of Erhai Lake. From here, you can see the entire lake, with the nineteen peaks of Cangshan Mountain reflected on the water, a spectacular sight.
attractions.tips: It is most beautiful at sunrise and sunset. It is recommended to drive there, and you can also cycle along Huanhai East Road.

attractions.name: 喜洲粑粑
attractions.description: Xizhou baba is the most famous specialty snack in Dali. It is baked over charcoal fire, crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, with both sweet and savory flavors. There are many shops in Xizhou Ancient Town that make Xizhou baba, and visitors can watch the making process on site.
attractions.address: Sifang Street, Xizhou Town, Dali City
attractions.tips: Be sure to eat it while it's hot; the freshly baked ones are the best. I recommend the time-honored shops on Sifang Street.

attractions.name: 周城扎染村
attractions.description: Zhoucheng Village is the birthplace of Bai tie-dye and is known as the 'Hometown of Bai Tie-dye.' Almost every household in the village is engaged in tie-dye production. Visitors can tour tie-dye workshops and try the craft themselves.
attractions.address: Zhoucheng Village, Xizhou Town, Dali City
attractions.tips: You can make your own tie-dye piece, priced at about 50-100 yuan. It's recommended to go in the morning to see the complete production process.

attractions.name: 双廊艺术区
attractions.description: Shuanglang is an artistic town by Erhai Lake, home to many artists and bohemians. The town features various art studios, galleries, and specialty shops, making it the most culturally vibrant area in Dali.
attractions.tips: It's recommended to stay overnight to catch the sunrise over Erhai Lake. The town has many distinctive guesthouses and cafés.

attractions.name: 洱海骑行
attractions.description: Cycling around Erhai Lake is one of the most popular tourist activities in Dali. The full loop is about 130 kilometers, offering views of the lake's scenery, Bai villages, and pastoral landscapes along the way—the best way to experience Dali in depth.
attractions.address: Erhai Lake Ring Road, Dali City
attractions.tips: It's recommended to cycle clockwise, which takes about 2 days in total. There are several supply points along the way. Remember to protect yourself from the sun and stay hydrated.

attractions.name: 三塔倒影
attractions.description: The reflection of the Three Pagodas is one of Dali's most famous sights. In the pond in front of the pagodas, their reflections are clearly visible, creating a charming contrast with the real pagodas, especially at dawn and dusk.
attractions.address: Within the Chongsheng Temple and Three Pagodas Scenic Area, Dali City
attractions.tips: It is most beautiful in the morning when there is mist, and the reflection is clearest when the water is calm. It is recommended to go in the morning.

attractions.name: 南诏风情岛
attractions.description: Nanzhao Customs Island is an important tourist attraction on Erhai Lake. The island features the Nanzhao Palace, the Bai People's Benzhu Culture Square, and more, showcasing the history and culture of the Nanzhao Kingdom. It is an important window to understand the history of Dali.
attractions.address: In the middle of Erhai Lake, Shuanglang Town, Dali City
attractions.tips: You need to take a boat to the island, and it is recommended to check the weather in advance. There are Bai ethnic song and dance performances on the island.

attractions.name: 挖色集市
attractions.description: Wase Market is a traditional Bai ethnic market on the east bank of Erhai Lake. On market days, villagers from the surrounding areas gather here to trade agricultural products and handicrafts, making it a great place to experience rural life of the Bai people.
attractions.openingHours: Market days (on the 5th and 10th of each month)
attractions.tips: Market days are the most lively, where you can see various local specialties and handicrafts. It is recommended to go in the morning.

attractions.name: 石门关
attractions.description: Shimen Pass is a natural canyon on the west slope of Cangshan Mountain. The cliffs on both sides are as steep as a gate, and a stream flows gently at the bottom. It is a rare canyon landscape in Dali and a paradise for hiking enthusiasts.
attractions.address: West slope of Cangshan Mountain, Dali City
attractions.tips: It is recommended to wear non-slip shoes, as the canyon is relatively cool. Pay attention to safety during the rainy season.

attractions.name: 无为寺
attractions.description: Wuwei Temple is located at the eastern foot of Cangshan Mountain's Lanfeng Peak. First built in the Tang Dynasty, it is a renowned Buddhist temple in Dali. The temple grounds are tranquil, with ancient trees reaching for the sky and several thousand-year-old camellia trees, making it an ideal place for locals to cultivate their minds and bodies.
attractions.address: Eastern foot of Lanfeng Peak, Cangshan Mountain, Dali City
attractions.tips: Spring (January to March) is the most beautiful time when the camellias are in full bloom. The temple offers vegetarian meals.

attractions.name: 喜洲古镇
attractions.description: The best-preserved ancient town of Bai architecture, featuring representative buildings such as the Yan Family Grand Courtyard.
attractions.tips: Try Xizhou baba (a local savory or sweet flatbread).

attractions.name: 大理古城夜景
attractions.description: Night views of Dali Old Town, with Renmin Road and Foreigner Street brightly lit.
attractions.tips: Experience Dali's nightlife.
